description: Math-15 batchB: M11-M15, renumbered P01-P05; original id in screen_id. prompt = game-framed wording, neutral_twin = plain math. Built by tools/build_math15.py.

rubric.M1: Final answer matches the answer key (exact, or within stated rounding) - must
rubric.M2: Sets up the right model (sample space, independence, conditioning, optimal-play recursion) - must
rubric.M3: No calculation errors in the steps - should
rubric.M4: Each step follows from the previous one (no leap to the answer) - should
rubric.M5: States the assumptions it makes - should

prompts.prompt: You open random sticker packs with one sticker each and 10 equally common designs; derive the exact expected number of packs needed to collect all 10.
prompts.neutral_twin: Draws are uniform and independent over 10 types. What is the exact expected number of draws until every type has appeared at least once?

R: Splits into stages with geometric waits of mean 10/(10 - k)

prompts.prompt: In a cooking game, you have five minutes and can make a 2-minute dish worth 3 points or a 3-minute dish worth 5 points with a 20% chance of burning for 0 points; derive the optimal plan when you can adapt after each dish.
prompts.neutral_twin: You have 5 time units. Task A takes 2 units and earns 3. Task B takes 3 units and earns 5 with probability 0.8, else 0. Tasks run one at a time and you may choose after each result. What plan maximizes the expected score, and what is it?
prompts.answer_key: Make one of each, in either order: expected 3 + 0.8 * 5 = 7. Two 2-minute dishes give only 6, and two 3-minute dishes don't fit. Adapting doesn't change the plan.
prompts.assumptions: A dish must finish within the 5 minutes; risk-neutral (expected points).

R: Final answer: one of each dish (either order), expected 7 points
Lists the feasible plans (AA = 6, AB/BA = 7, BB doesn't fit)
Notes the burn outcome doesn't change the next choice

prompts.prompt: A wizard flips a fair coin until either HHT or THH appears; derive the exact probability that HHT appears first, accounting for overlapping sequences.
prompts.neutral_twin: A fair coin is flipped until HHT or THH appears as three consecutive flips. What is the exact probability that HHT appears first?
prompts.answer_key: 1/4. HHT wins only if the first two flips are HH; once a T has appeared, THH must come before HHT.

R: Argument: after any T, the first HH is preceded by T, so THH comes first; HHT needs HH at the start

prompts.prompt: A spaceship gets three independent repair attempts, each restoring one system with probability 2/3; derive the exact chance of restoring at least two systems and the expected number restored.
prompts.neutral_twin: X ~ Binomial(3, 2/3). Find P(X >= 2) and E[X] exactly.

prompts.prompt: In Connect Four, both players choose uniformly among legal columns on every turn; derive the exact probability that the first player wins on their fourth move, without simulation.
prompts.neutral_twin: On a standard 6-row by 7-column Connect Four board, both players drop pieces in a uniformly random legal column each turn. What is the exact probability that the first player completes four in a row on their fourth move (move 7 overall)?
prompts.assumptions: Computed by exact enumeration of all 7^7 move sequences with legal-column weighting. Player 2 cannot have won by then (only 3 pieces).

R: Sets up the count over 7^7 equally likely sequences and the line types (horizontal, vertical, diagonal)
Notes player 2 cannot win before move 7

prompts.notes: Very hard to do by hand; an honest approximate method with a clearly stated estimate should pass M2-M5 even if M1 fails.
